goal: Confirm the frozen Block publication and exit-settlement product contract without introducing source syntax or a managed runtime.
description: Scope: Requirements.md, Plan.md, and the P01.12-A..B / O05-Q06 decision trace. Context: the owner has frozen publication after required settlement, one static dependency graph, internal total/fallible/fatal classification, and compiler-sized fixed failure slots. Target: keep REQ-BE-001..REQ-BE-008 complete, source-observable where effects and diagnostics require it, and explicit that all graph/storage names remain compiler-only. Design Considerations: requirements describe one final contract and preserve the parent Block-result algebra; they distinguish implementation-hidden representation from statically visible failure effects. Design Value: prevents implementation details from inventing syntax, hiding physical failure, or reopening the decision. Constraints & Risks: do not reopen decided D02 or add ordinary value fallback; new cancellation APIs, transactions, and resource completion levels remain outside this plan; shared substrate belongs to styio-common-foundation.

acceptance_criteria.text: Requirements.md states users, scope, non-goals, constraints, and final acceptance for REQ-BE-001..REQ-BE-008.
Every requirement traces to P01.12-A..B/O05-Q06 and explicitly preserves the no-new-syntax, no-managed-runtime, and honest-effect boundaries.

goal: Verify repository exit-path gaps, historical failure lessons, and the data-structure basis for a runtime-free protocol.
description: Scope: Evidence.md plus read-only inspection of StyioResourceTopology, Sema, StyioIR, lowering, codegen, accepted task/resource hooks, tests, and active docs. Context: current exits use family-split cleanup, hash-derived commit enumeration, construct-specific control flow, and first-error-only support state. Target: cite exact symbols and primary language/compiler lessons supporting dependency ordering, candidate ownership, fixed failure slots, bounded children, and handler-after-epilogue semantics. Design Considerations: compare reverse-drop defaults, native compiler-generated cleanup, typed-failure loss, double-failure termination, structured join, and deterministic scheduling; distinguish evidence from inference. Design Value: grounds every graph, storage, complexity, and failure choice before implementation. Constraints & Risks: external mechanisms provide failure history and patterns only; undecided lexical features, Java runtime representation, and any unbounded heap strategy remain forbidden.

acceptance_criteria.text: Evidence.md cites every current implementation path that orders, commits, releases, joins, publishes, or records Block exit failure.
Evidence.md compares relevant systems-language and compiler practices and derives the chosen dense DAG, stable schedule, fixed-slot, and bounded-child consequences.

goal: Define deterministic, ownership, multi-failure, no-runtime, and convergence evidence before implementation.
description: Scope: Validation.md and read-only test/gate discovery. Context: a shallow natural-exit test can pass while yield, loop control, failure, concurrency, resource borrowing, or generated storage still violates the contract. Target: map every REQ-BE label to positive, negative, verifier, structural, randomized, concurrent, sanitizer, and final end-to-end checks. Design Considerations: require exact source spans and stable ordinals; cover N==0, declared bounds, one-past-bound rejection, body-plus-cleanup failures, accepted task/resource edges, conditional integration for later admitted frame-retaining features, and unchanged token/grammar inventories. Design Value: makes determinism, bounded memory, and failure preservation testable before code shapes bias acceptance. Constraints & Risks: commands must name existing suites or explicitly identify tests to add; prose review alone cannot satisfy a criterion.

acceptance_criteria.text: Validation.md maps every REQ-BE label to executable or structural evidence, including randomized order and concurrent completion stress.
The matrix proves no new syntax/runtime mechanism, fixed bounded storage, honest total/fallible/fatal classification, complete migration, and deterministic diagnostics.

goal: Freeze the exit graph, verified IR, fixed failure layout, module split, and no-runtime lowering architecture.
description: Scope: Architecture.md and the interface/scaffold contract for new ExitActionGraph, SGExit, ExitProtocolVerifier, ExitProtocolLowering, and ExitProtocolCodeGen responsibilities. Context: ResourceTopology validates metadata without emitting a schedule, while large shared lowering/codegen files separately infer partial cleanup. Target: define dense action IDs, compact adjacency, deterministic Kahn scheduling, candidate ownership, action outcome classes, fixed child/failure segments, direct handler CFG, final sinks, module boundaries, and dependency direction. Design Considerations: graph build O(V+E), stable scheduling O(V log V+E), cached schedule consumption, one responsibility per new file, verifier firewall, and thin native-hook adapters. Design Value: moves semantic proof out of backend guesses and preserves every typed failure without heap/runtime machinery. Constraints & Risks: do not create parser/AST surface, global failure objects, dynamic dispatch, duplicate scheduling authority, or compatibility files; architecture changes discovered later must be recorded before coupled code changes.

acceptance_criteria.text: Architecture.md defines module/file ownership, dependency direction, interfaces, state machines, graph/layout data structures, algorithms, complexity, and final sinks.
Each deliberate pattern explains its value, source syntax remains pattern-free, and no new file combines unrelated graph, verifier, lowering, codegen, and native-hook responsibilities.

goal: Build and verify the semantic per-Block exit-action dependency graph and stable schedule.
description: Scope: StyioSema exit facts, src/StyioResourceTopology/ExitActionGraph.hpp/.cpp, minimal ResourceTopology integration, topology/Sema tests, and graph diagnostics. Context: current topology records useful ownership, borrow, commit, and HB edges but does not include all of them in cycle detection or emit an executable order. Target: classify actions and bounds, build dense per-Block action/edge storage, deduplicate edges, derive lifetime/commit/hook dependencies, reconstruct source-located cycles, compute and cache the deterministic ready-queue schedule and semantic ordinals, and mark safe concurrency batches. Design Considerations: one O(V+E) graph build, O(V log V+E) stable Kahn schedule, compact IDs/adjacency, no pointer/hash ordering, and no codegen reanalysis. Design Value: turns existing semantic facts into one deterministic proof consumed by every exit path. Constraints & Risks: no native storage or handler syntax is chosen here; parent Block-result typing and separately declared resource/task contracts remain authoritative.

acceptance_criteria.text: Topology/Sema tests cover every edge family, deterministic reverse-registration tie-breaking, dependency override, edge deduplication, declared bounds, and source-located relevant cycles.
Randomized insertion/hash-order tests produce identical schedules, ordinals, batches, and diagnostics, with measured graph and scheduling complexity matching Architecture.md.
Code inspection proves the schedule is built and cached once per Block and contains no pointer-identity or unordered-container ordering authority.

goal: Represent and verify the sealed candidate, exit actions, fixed failure layout, and final sinks in StyioIR and lowering.
description: Scope: src/StyioIR/GenIR/SGExit.hpp, src/StyioIR/ExitProtocolVerifier.*, minimal IR walker/declaration integration, src/StyioLowering/ExitProtocolLowering.*, and IR/lowering tests. Context: SGBlock/SGReturn currently conflate result and exit behavior, and lowering validates topology without carrying an exit schedule or bounded failure layout. Target: add typed exit IR that owns candidate metadata, action descriptors, stable schedule/batches, total/fallible/fatal outcomes, slot/child bounds, commit-or-abort reason, and publish/branch/propagate/fatal sink; lower every source exit edge to it. Design Considerations: the verifier rejects malformed ownership, edges, ordinals, layout, unbounded obligations, illegal sinks, and handler-before-seal; lowering consumes Sema/RTG proof and never rebuilds topology. Design Value: establishes a hard semantic firewall before native code generation. Constraints & Risks: avoid growing the generic Verifier.cpp with unrelated logic; no source token, heap layout, runtime object, or dynamic handler search may appear.

acceptance_criteria.text: IR verifier tests accept each valid exit reason/sink and reject early publication, double owner, dying borrow, illegal commit/abort, duplicate ordinal/slot, unbounded child, and handler-before-seal forms.
Lowering tests prove natural, yield, function, loop-control, typed-failure, and cancellation edges produce the same exit protocol form and consume the cached semantic schedule.
IR dumps retain nominal completion families and fixed bounds while adding no parser, token, AST exception, or authored classification surface.

goal: Emit allocation-free candidate settlement, fixed multi-failure state, stable concurrency, and direct effect-handler control flow.
description: Scope: src/StyioCodeGen/ExitProtocolCodeGen.*, fixed-layout helpers owned by that module, codegen/IR goldens, concurrency stress, security, and allocation-structure tests. Context: current global support state keeps only one error and cannot preserve bounded typed failures or deterministic concurrent ordering. Target: emit epilogue-owned candidate storage, no ledger for N==0, fixed bit/inline-payload slots for fallible actions and child segments, O(1) direct failure stores, semantic-ordinal primary/secondary selection, sealed handler routing by direct CFG, explicit replacement recovery, and publish/branch/propagate/fatal sinks. Design Considerations: stack or preallocated contiguous storage only; slot liveness reuse requires verifier proof; concurrency batches retain preassigned ordinals and never use completion time. Design Value: preserves complete typed evidence with deterministic behavior and no managed runtime or heap allocation. Constraints & Risks: support logging is non-authoritative; a physically fallible hook cannot be silently reclassified total; fatal inability remains outside recoverable aggregation.

acceptance_criteria.text: Generated-code tests prove N==0 emits no ledger and bounded fallible cases use only fixed stack/preallocated status and inline payload slots.
Body-plus-cleanup, multiple-child, cancellation, timeout/join, candidate-discard, and concurrent-race tests preserve deterministic primary and every secondary failure.
Structural inspection proves no malloc/new/GC, exception object, growable list, dynamic handler search, global typed failure append, or scheduler-based ordering exists.

goal: Migrate every concrete exit path and lifecycle hook to the one verified protocol and delete old ordering authorities.
description: Scope: existing exit/cleanup code in src/StyioCodeGen/CodeGenG.cpp and CodeGenIO.cpp, concrete accepted task/resource hooks in src/StyioExtern, pending commit/flush/release paths, affected tests, and deletion of obsolete helpers. Context: natural Block, yield, functions, loops, break/continue, runtime errors, and cleanup errors currently perform different partial actions; family passes and first-error state can still decide behavior. Target: route all edges through ExitProtocolCodeGen, expose honest fixed status from concrete hooks, enforce join-before-borrowed-release and every admitted feature's proven terminal-before-release edge, select commit versus abort by exit reason, preserve earlier barriers, and leave each owner exactly one cleanup path. Design Considerations: existing hooks remain thin adapters; a cancellation request never substitutes for join; family-specific operations cannot impose global order; irreversible I/O is not rolled back. Design Value: removes path drift and makes the frozen protocol the only executable authority. Constraints & Risks: complete migration is mandatory in one change set; no undecided continuation integration, old/legacy/fallback epilogue, default-return repair, double release, or positive test for retired behavior remains.

acceptance_criteria.text: End-to-end tests prove every exit reason uses the same protocol, success commits, failure aborts only unpublished state, and ordinary results never publish before non-transferable obligations finish.

Resource/task tests prove join/commit/flush/close dependencies, exactly-one cleanup ownership, honest hook failure, and no implicit detach or fake rollback; later admitted features add conditional integration tests through their own plans.
Static deletion evidence finds no construct-specific epilogue authority, family-global ordering pass, default-result repair, or first-error-only canonical propagation in exit paths.

goal: Converge active language/resource documentation, diagnostics, fixtures, test catalogs, and tooling on the runtime-free exit contract.
description: Scope: Styio Language Design, Resource Topology, Block-completion/stream design docs, active syntax mirrors, Sema/IR/codegen/test runbooks, test catalog, syntax decision report links, diagnostics, fixtures, and generated indexes. Context: active prose still describes reverse-only cleanup, infallible sessions, Java-style suppression, construct-specific behavior, or undecided continuation semantics, while syntax mirrors must prove no token change. Target: publish one dependency-first, fixed-native-state contract, update tests and runbooks to current behavior, migrate/remove obsolete fixtures, and link the child plan from its parent and decision register. Design Considerations: language/resource SSOT owns semantics; syntax mirrors assert no new authored form; generated indexes are regenerated; only current negative diagnostics remain for removed paths. Design Value: prevents old runtime assumptions or hidden syntax from surviving as documentation and acceptance debt. Constraints & Risks: do not retain historical implementation labels or compatibility tests; do not activate continuations, reopen D02, or introduce a fallback operator, cancellation API, transaction rollback, or new resource completion levels.

acceptance_criteria.text: All active language/resource/Block-completion/stream docs and runbooks state the same publication, dependency-order, fixed-failure, fatal, no-runtime, and no-unapproved-continuation rules.
Tokenizer, EBNF, symbol, and active-syntax evidence proves this plan added no source token, keyword, constructor, exception type, or authored total/fallible/fatal classification.
Obsolete executable fixtures and compatibility expectations are removed, generated indexes are current, and syntax-convergence, docs, lifecycle, local-information, and plan gates pass.

goal: Prove the complete Block exit publication and settlement contract on one head commit.
description: Scope: execute and record every Validation.md mapping; source fixes route back to their owning implementation node. Context: topology, IR, codegen, native hooks, resource/task behavior, concurrency, diagnostics, and docs can each pass locally while disagreeing end to end. Target: run all targeted and standing checks, randomized/hash/concurrency determinism stress, allocation/static audits, obsolete-authority searches, syntax inventory comparison, and Better Plan validation on one commit. Design Considerations: evidence must cover source behavior, ownership/lifetime, IR verification, native layout, failure order, fatal behavior, complexity, concurrency, migration deletion, and documentation together. Design Value: turns the frozen owner decision into auditable delivery rather than a prose-only promise. Constraints & Risks: acceptance targets cannot be weakened around unrelated worktree failures; decided D02 must not be reopened, and resource/cancellation/transaction choices remain out of scope and fail closed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Build, targeted topology/Sema/IR/codegen/resource/task tests, conditional tests for already admitted lexical features, randomized/concurrent stress, sanitizer/security, syntax-convergence, documentation, lifecycle, local-information, and plan validators pass on one head commit.
Every REQ-BE label has recorded positive, negative, structural, determinism, complexity, and source-location evidence from Validation.md.

No new source syntax, managed runtime mechanism, dynamic allocation fallback, construct-specific epilogue, hidden physical failure, obsolete acceptance fixture, or contradictory active documentation remains.
